name: Jared Galloway
summary: Bioinformatician and ML scientist with nine years of experience building pipelines, models, and research software for sequencing data. Work spans Nextflow and Snakemake workflows on HPC clusters and AWS, genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and influenza, and transformers and sparse statistical models in PyTorch and JAX. Co-author of more than 20 publications with 1,800+ citations.
bio: I build bioinformatics pipelines, machine learning models, and the software that puts them to work on noisy, high-dimensional sequencing data. I hold a B.S. in Computer & Information Science and an M.S. in Biology. Over nine years, I have developed methods in research groups at HHMI, Fred Hutch, and the University of Oregon.

I work across the whole analysis lifecycle and the infrastructure around it: processing raw sequencing data in reproducible Nextflow and Snakemake workflows, fitting models in PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow, validating them on simulated and experimental data, and shipping open-source packages and pipelines that run at scale on HPC clusters and AWS. My [skills page](https://jaredgalloway.com/skills/) shows where I've used each tool.

That work has contributed to more than 20 publications with 1,800+ citations, in journals including *Cell*, *eLife*, and *Molecular Biology and Evolution*. My [research page](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/) collects the papers that best represent it, with figures, code, and documentation. Most recently, I built transformer models of natural selection in viral proteins. My [experience page](https://jaredgalloway.com/experience/) covers each role in detail.

I left the Matsen Lab in August 2026 and am looking for my next role in bioinformatics or applied machine learning. I take pride in clearly communicating my work and enjoy the discussions that follow.
